Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Alabama, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 27Passed

An application sent by mail must be received by the Absentee Election Manager no later than 7 days before the election: Tuesday, October 27, 2026. An application handed in must be received no later than 5 days before: Thursday, October 29, 2026. Emergency applications (for example, an unexpected work requirement or a death in the family within five days of the election) can be made until 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

A ballot sent by mail must be received by the Absentee Election Manager no later than noon on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A ballot handed in must be in the office by the close of business (no later than 5 p.m.) on Monday, November 2, 2026. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. When and where to vote early.

Alabama’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Alabama or in another state? What Alabama says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

You need one of the reasons the state lists: you expect to be away from your county on Election Day; you are ill or have a physical disability that keeps you from the polls; you are 65 or older or have a disability and cannot get into your polling place; you are a registered Alabama voter living outside your county (such as a member of the armed forces, someone working outside the United States, a college student, or the spouse or child of one); you are an election officer or poll watcher at another polling place; you must work a shift of 10 hours or more during voting hours; you care for a close family member confined at home; or you are in jail or prison and have not been convicted of a felony involving moral turpitude. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Write to your county's Absentee Election Manager (usually the Circuit Clerk), or use the state's absentee application form. Give your name and home address, the election, your reason, the address to mail the ballot to, and your original signature (electronic signatures are not accepted), and include a copy of your valid photo ID. Send it by U.S. mail or a delivery company; each voter's application must go in its own envelope. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Visit your county's Absentee Election Manager and hand in the application yourself, with a copy of your photo ID. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Send it by U.S. mail, to arrive by noon on Election Day. (official page)
  • By mail. Send it by a commercial delivery company, to arrive by noon on Election Day. (official page)
  • In person. Hand your own ballot to the Absentee Election Manager by 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2. Only in an emergency absentee case may someone you name deliver it for you. The state lists these as the only legal ways to return a ballot. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Include a copy of your valid photo ID with your application. After you vote, seal the ballot in the envelope, put that in the envelope with the oath printed on it, and sign the oath. Your signature must be witnessed either by a notary public or by two witnesses who are 18 or older; a ballot without this is not counted. Electronic or remote notarizing is not allowed. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Alabama’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

The Secretary of State's absentee page describes no separate early voting period. If you have one of the listed reasons, you can visit the Absentee Election Manager, apply in person (by Thursday, October 29, 2026), and the manager may hand you the ballot there; a ballot handed in must be in by 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2. (official page)

Students

At school in Alabama, away from home

The state lists college students living outside the county where they are registered as able to vote absentee. A student registered at home who lives at school in another Alabama county can apply for an absentee ballot and have it mailed to school. The Secretary of State's absentee page does not say which address a student may register at. (official page)

At school in another state, with Alabama as home

The same rule applies: a registered Alabama voter living outside the county, such as a college student, may vote absentee, so a student at school in another state can ask for an Alabama absentee ballot mailed there. The Secretary of State's absentee page does not speak to where a student's residence is. (official page)

Military and overseas

Members of the uniformed services and their families, the merchant marine and Alabama citizens overseas can choose to get their ballot for federal offices electronically, by regular mail or by commercial carrier. For November 3, 2026, the federal guide says registration must be postmarked by October 19 (that date has passed), the ballot request received by Tuesday, October 27, and a mailed ballot postmarked by Election Day and received by Tuesday, November 10 (the 7th day after). (federal guide)

Alabama in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The Secretary of State gives the deadlines as rules (7 days before, 5 days before, the day before); the dates here were worked out for November 3, 2026.
  • No online application was found on the Secretary of State's absentee page; the application needs an original signature.
  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program's state guide was read through the content feed its own page loads.
Where this comes from: 2 pages of Alabama’s election office, its laws and the federal guide

  2. Voting Assistance Guide, chapter 2: Alabama, Federal Voting Assistance Program (federal guide; read October 21, 2026)
